The SEISd module for the XH component

Source: R/human-XH-SEISd.R
SEISd.Rd

Implements the XH component using a delay Susceptible-Exposed-Infectious-Susceptible (SEISd) model of human infection dynamics. This is a delay differential equation version of the SEIS model, in which the exposed period is modelled as a fixed delay \(\nu\) rather than an exponential rate.

Note

In SEISd, mass treatment clears infectious individuals, returning them to susceptibility; exposed individuals and exposure history are unaffected.

State Variables

H

total human (or host) population density

E

density of exposed (infected but not yet infectious) humans

I

density of infectious humans

S=H-E-I

density of susceptible humans or hosts

cases

cumulative exposures used to track delayed progression

This implementation includes human demographic change, progressive stratification, and parameters to model detection by diagnostic methods. It also includes parameters for treating and curing infections and functions to model mass treatment.

Dynamical Term

\(h\) or foi

The force of infection is computed and stored by Exposure as FoI

In the SEISd module, there is no effect of pre-erythrocytic immunity, so a constant fraction of infectious bites causes an infection: the parameter \(b\).

Parameters

The parameters returned by get_XH_pars.SEISd and modifiable by change_XH_pars.SEISd describe the dynamics or detection by diagnostic methods.

b

transmission probability from mosquito to human

c

transmission probability from human to mosquito

nu

intrinsic incubation period (fixed delay, in days)

r

clearance rate for infections

rho or \(\rho\)

the fraction of incident infections that are treated and cured

sigma or \(\sigma\)

the rate that prevalent infections are treated and cured

q_lm

test positivity by light microscopy

q_rdt

test positivity by RDT

q_pcr

test positivity by PCR

Infection Dynamics

Infections clear naturally at the per-capita rate \(r\), after which individuals are susceptible to infection. Incident infections are delayed progression \(C(t)\), not new exposures \(hS\). A fraction \(\rho\) of incident infections are treated and cured, returning directly to susceptibility. Prevalent infections are treated and cured at rate \(\sigma\); mass treatment adds clearance at rate \(\Xi(t) = mda(t) + msat(t)\). Treatment does not change the exposed-state equation or exposure history, and does not add a \(\rho h\) clearance term. $$ \begin{array}{rl} dE/dt &= hS - C(t) - \mathbf{D}(E) \\ dI/dt &= (1-\rho)C(t) - (r+\sigma+\Xi(t))I - \mathbf{D}(I) \\ d\,\mathrm{cases}/dt &= hS \\ \end{array}$$ where \(h\) is the force of infection, \(S = H - E - I\), and \(C(t)\) is zero for \(t \leq \nu\); otherwise it is the rate of exposure \(h(t-\nu)S(t-\nu)\) recorded \(\nu\) days ago (computed via deSolve::lagderiv). The mortality function uses the same model for \(E\) and \(I\) as for \(H\). Susceptible density is redundant and is computed after solving.

Demography

This model has no parameter or terms to describe disease-induced mortality.

Births or \(\mathbf{B}\)

the births function

Deaths or \(\mathbf{D}\)

the deaths function

Setup:

The default is a constant population model: birth and death rates are set to zero

  • Use setup_births to configure Births

  • Use setup_deaths to configure Deaths

Also, see xds_info_demographic_change.

Prevalence

\(x\)

True prevalence is \(x = I/H\)

\(x_{lm}\)

Expected prevalence by light microscopy is \(q_{lm}\; x\)

\(x_{rdt}\)

Expected prevalence by RDT is \(q_{rdt}\; x\)

\(x_{pcr}\)

Expected prevalence by PCR is \(q_{pcr}\; x\)

These prevalence functions count infectious individuals, not exposed individuals.

Infectiousness

The probability that a mosquito becomes infected after feeding on an infectious host is \(c\). Infectious density is \(cI\), and net infectiousness is \(cI/H\).

Mass Treatment

Mass treatment clears infections. At basic setup \(\Xi(t)=0\). To set up mass treatment, see setup_mass_treatment. Mass treatment is either:

mda(t) or \(\Xi(t)\)

mass drug administration

msat(t) or \(\Xi(t)\)

mass screen and treat
